title: Abraham's journeys
summary: Abram leaves Ur with his father Terah, settles at Haran, then at God's call walks the length of Canaan, goes down to Egypt in famine, and returns to live by Hebron. His faith is tested on a mountain in the land of Moriah.

stops.note: Terah takes Abram, Sarai and Lot from Ur of the Chaldeans, heading for Canaan. Stephen says God first appeared to Abraham here.
The family settles in Haran and Terah dies there. God calls Abram, aged 75, to go to the land he will show him.
At the oak of Moreh God promises the land to Abram's offspring; Abram builds his first altar in Canaan.
Abram pitches his tent between Bethel and Ai and calls on the name of the LORD.
Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he presents Sarai as his sister; Pharaoh sends them away.
Abram returns through the Negev, rich in livestock, silver and gold; he and Lot later part ways.
Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron, receives the covenant promises, and later buries Sarah in the cave of Machpelah.
God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac on a mountain in the land of Moriah; a ram is provided instead.

title: Jacob's journeys
summary: Jacob flees from Esau to his uncle Laban in Paddan-aram, meeting God at Bethel on the way. Twenty years later he returns with a large family, wrestles with God at Peniel, settles in Canaan, and at the end of his life goes down to Egypt.

stops.note: Jacob leaves Beersheba after taking Esau's blessing.
He dreams of a stairway to heaven and vows to make the LORD his God.
At the well near Haran he meets Rachel and serves Laban fourteen years for his wives and six for his flocks.
In Paddan-aram eleven of his sons and his daughter Dinah are born; he leaves secretly for Canaan.
At the Jabbok he wrestles with a man until daybreak and is renamed Israel.
He buys land at Shechem and builds an altar; the violence against Dinah and the revenge of Simeon and Levi follow.
God calls him back to Bethel, where the family buries foreign gods and God renews the promise.
On the way to Ephrath (Bethlehem) Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin.
Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre/Hebron; Isaac dies and is buried by Esau and Jacob.
Setting out for Egypt, Jacob offers sacrifices at Beersheba and God tells him not to fear going down.
Jacob settles in Goshen, blesses Pharaoh and lives seventeen more years.

title: Joseph sold into Egypt
summary: Sent by his father to check on his brothers, Joseph follows them from Hebron to Shechem and Dothan, where they sell him to traders who carry him to Egypt.

stops.note: Jacob sends Joseph from the Valley of Hebron to see how his brothers are doing.
A man finds Joseph wandering near Shechem and tells him his brothers moved on.
The brothers throw him into a pit and sell him to Ishmaelite/Midianite traders for twenty shekels.
Joseph is sold to Potiphar, later imprisoned, and finally raised to rule Egypt under Pharaoh.

title: The exodus: southern Sinai route
summary: The traditional route, held since at least the fourth century: Israel crosses near the Gulf of Suez, travels down the west side of the Sinai peninsula to Jebel Musa (Mount Sinai at St. Catherine's Monastery), then north to Kadesh-barnea. Supporters point to the long monastic tradition and the eleven-day distance of Deut 1:2. The text names stations, not coordinates, and the location of the sea crossing and of Mount Sinai is uncertain. Three main reconstructions are shown as variants with equal weight.

stops.note: Israel sets out from Rameses in the eastern Delta the day after Passover.
First camp; then Etham on the edge of the wilderness. God leads them by the pillar of cloud and fire, not by the coastal "way of the Philistines."
On this view the crossing is at the northern tip of the Gulf of Suez or the Bitter Lakes.
Three days without water; the bitter water is made sweet.
Twelve springs and seventy palms, often placed at Wadi Gharandel.
Manna and quail are given.
Water from the rock and victory over Amalek while Moses' hands are held up.
Mount Sinai identified with Jebel Musa in the south of the peninsula; the law is given and Israel camps nearly a year.
Eleven days' journey from Horeb, Israel reaches Kadesh and sends the spies.

title: The exodus: northern route
summary: A northern reconstruction: the "sea" is one of the lagoons or lakes along the northern Sinai (e.g. Lake Bardawil) or the Bitter Lakes, and Mount Sinai is sought in the north-central Sinai or Negev (proposals include Jebel Sin Bishar, Jebel Helal and Har Karkom), closer to Kadesh-barnea. Supporters note that Kadesh was Israel's long-term base and that Egyptian forts guarded the coast road. Critics note that Exod 13:17 says God did not lead them by the coastal road. The text names stations, not coordinates, and the location of the sea crossing and of Mount Sinai is uncertain. Three main reconstructions are shown as variants with equal weight.

stops.note: Departure from Rameses (often identified with Pi-Ramesses/Qantir).
Succoth, possibly Tjeku in the Wadi Tumilat.
On this view the crossing is at a northern marshy lake ("Sea of Reeds").
Bitter water, placed on this route in the northern Shur wilderness.
Manna and quail in the wilderness between Elim and Sinai.
Mount Sinai located in north-central Sinai or the Negev highlands rather than at Jebel Musa; the map pin shows the traditional site, so read this stop as an alternative identification.
Kadesh-barnea (Ain el-Qudeirat), close to the northern candidates for Sinai.

title: The exodus: Midian / Arabia route
summary: An Arabian reconstruction: Israel crosses the Sinai peninsula to the Gulf of Aqaba (the "Red Sea" crossing at Nuweiba or the Straits of Tiran) into Midian, and Mount Sinai is in north-west Arabia (often Jebel al-Lawz). Supporters cite Moses meeting God near Midian, Jethro living nearby, and Paul's "Mount Sinai in Arabia." Critics reply that "Arabia" in Paul's day included Sinai, that the Aqaba crossing is too far for the timeline, and that claimed physical evidence at Jebel al-Lawz is disputed. The text names stations, not coordinates, and the location of the sea crossing and of Mount Sinai is uncertain. Three main reconstructions are shown as variants with equal weight.

stops.note: Departure from Rameses.
First camp at Succoth.
On this view the crossing is the Gulf of Aqaba, an arm of the Red Sea (yam suph also names the Aqaba gulf in 1 Kgs 9:26).
Israel enters Midian, the land where Moses had lived with Jethro and first met God at the bush.
Mount Sinai interpreted as a mountain in Arabia, often Jebel al-Lawz; the map pin shows the traditional site, so read this stop as an alternative identification.
Israel later moves north to Kadesh-barnea.

title: From Sinai to the plains of Moab
summary: After a year at Sinai Israel moves to Kadesh, fails to enter the land, and spends a generation in the wilderness. Refused passage by Edom, they go around it, defeat Sihon and Og, and camp on the plains of Moab opposite Jericho.

stops.note: The cloud lifts in the second year and Israel sets out by tribes.
The spies' report and the people's refusal; forty years of wandering decreed. Miriam later dies here.
Edom refuses passage on the King's Highway; Aaron dies at Mount Hor on the border; the bronze serpent.
Israel camps on the plains of Moab; Balaam is hired to curse them but blesses instead; Moses gives the speeches of Deuteronomy.
Moses views the land from Nebo and dies.

title: The conquest under Joshua
summary: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan, takes Jericho and Ai, renews the covenant at Shechem, wins campaigns in the south and north, and sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh. Dates follow the early or late exodus and the scale of conquest is debated archaeologically.

stops.note: Spies go out from Shittim on the plains of Moab.
Rahab hides the spies.
The river stops as the priests' feet touch the water.
Twelve memorial stones; circumcision and Passover; the manna ceases.
The walls fall after seven days of marching.
Defeat because of Achan's sin, then victory by ambush.
Blessings and curses read at Mount Ebal and Gerizim.
Southern campaign after the defense of Gibeon: Lachish and other cities taken.
Northern coalition defeated; Hazor burned.
The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh and the land is allotted.
Joshua's farewell covenant: "choose this day whom you will serve."

title: David's flight from Saul
summary: Hunted by a jealous Saul, David flees from the court at Gibeah, hides in caves and wilderness strongholds, spares Saul's life twice, and finally takes refuge among the Philistines until Saul's death opens the way to the throne.

stops.note: Saul throws his spear at David; Michal helps him escape through a window.
David flees to Samuel at Naioth in Ramah; Saul's messengers prophesy.
He seeks refuge with Achish of Gath and feigns madness.
His family and four hundred distressed men gather to him at the cave of Adullam.
David cuts the corner of Saul's robe in a cave but spares him.
Achish gives him Ziklag; it is raided by Amalekites and David strengthens himself in God.
After Saul dies, David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron.

title: Elijah's flight to Horeb
summary: After the contest on Carmel, Jezebel threatens Elijah. He runs south to Beersheba and the wilderness, is fed by an angel, walks forty days to Horeb, and is sent back north, where he calls Elisha.

stops.note: Fire falls on the altar and the prophets of Baal are killed.
Elijah runs ahead of Ahab's chariot to Jezreel; Jezebel vows to kill him.
He leaves his servant at Beersheba and goes a day's journey into the wilderness, where an angel feeds him.
At the mountain of God he hears the low whisper and is commissioned again.
He throws his cloak over Elisha, who is plowing with twelve yoke of oxen.

title: Jonah's journey
summary: Told to preach against Nineveh, Jonah takes ship for Tarshish in the opposite direction, is thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, then goes to Nineveh, whose people repent.

stops.note: Jonah boards a ship at Joppa bound for Tarshish, "away from the presence of the LORD."
After the fish, he walks into the great city crying "Yet forty days"; the city repents and God relents, to Jonah's anger.

title: Exile to Babylon
summary: Judah's leaders are deported in waves (605, 597, 586 BC). The usual route ran north from Jerusalem through Syria to Nebuchadnezzar's headquarters at Riblah and then down the Euphrates to Babylon, avoiding the desert.

stops.note: Jerusalem is taken and burned; the people are carried away.
The road north through Syria toward Riblah, where Zedekiah's sons are killed before his eyes. The exact route is a reconstruction.
The exiles are settled in Babylonia; Jeremiah urges them to seek the welfare of the city.
Exiles live by the Chebar canal, where Ezekiel sees his visions.

title: Return under Ezra and Nehemiah
summary: After Zerubbabel's first return (538 BC), Ezra leads a second group from Babylon in 458 BC (or 398 BC on an alternative dating), and Nehemiah later travels from the Persian court at Susa to rebuild Jerusalem's walls (445 BC).

stops.note: Ezra sets out on the first day of the first month with the king's letter and gifts for the temple.
Ezra arrives after four months, deals with mixed marriages, and later reads the Law.
Nehemiah, cupbearer at the citadel of Susa, hears of the broken walls and is sent by Artaxerxes.
Nehemiah inspects the walls by night and the work is finished in fifty-two days.

title: The holy family: Nazareth, Bethlehem, Egypt
summary: Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem for the census, present Jesus in the temple, flee to Egypt from Herod, and return to settle in Nazareth. Luke and Matthew each tell part of the story.

stops.note: Gabriel announces Jesus' birth to Mary in Nazareth.
Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem, the city of David, for the registration; Jesus is born and laid in a manger.
Jesus is presented in the temple; Simeon and Anna recognize him.
The magi worship the child in a house in Bethlehem.
Warned in a dream, Joseph takes the child and his mother to Egypt until Herod dies: "Out of Egypt I called my son."
Avoiding Archelaus in Judea, the family settles in Nazareth in Galilee.

title: Jesus' Galilean ministry
summary: From his baptism to his decision to go up to Jerusalem, Jesus works mainly around the Sea of Galilee, based at Capernaum, with forays into Gentile territory. The gospels arrange episodes topically as well as chronologically, so this order is approximate.

stops.note: Baptized by John; the Spirit descends.
Water turned to wine, the first sign.
He reads Isaiah 61 in the synagogue and is rejected by his hometown.
He makes Capernaum his base, calls fishermen, heals Peter's mother-in-law and a paralytic, and calls Matthew.
Teaching from a boat; calming the storm.
He frees the Gerasene demoniac, who then proclaims him in the Decapolis.
He raises a widow's son at Nain.
Feeding of the five thousand near Bethsaida; walking on the water.
In the region of Tyre and Sidon he heals the Syrophoenician woman's daughter.
Peter confesses him as the Christ; Jesus foretells his death.
Transfiguration on a high mountain (traditionally Tabor; some argue Hermon).
Back in Capernaum he teaches the disciples about greatness and childlike faith.

title: Jesus' final journey to Jerusalem
summary: Jesus "set his face to go to Jerusalem," travelling through Perea and Jericho to Bethany, entering the city at Passover, and going to the cross.

stops.note: He leaves Galilee for the last time.
He teaches in Judea beyond the Jordan (Perea).
Bartimaeus receives sight; Zacchaeus receives Jesus.
Mary anoints him at Bethany six days before the Passover.
He rides down the Mount of Olives on a colt, weeping over the city.
He clears the temple, teaches, and shares the Last Supper with the Twelve.
He prays in anguish and is arrested.
Crucified outside the city, he dies and is buried nearby.

title: The road to Emmaus
summary: On resurrection day two disciples walking to Emmaus are joined by the risen Jesus, who explains the scriptures; they recognize him in the breaking of bread and hurry back to Jerusalem.

stops.note: Two disciples, one named Cleopas, leave Jerusalem discussing the events.
About seven miles away, Jesus is made known to them as he breaks bread. The village's location is uncertain.
They return the same hour and find the Eleven saying, "The Lord has risen indeed."

title: Philip the evangelist
summary: Scattered by persecution, Philip preaches in Samaria, is sent to the desert road to Gaza where he baptizes the Ethiopian official, then preaches along the coast to Caesarea, where he later hosts Paul.

stops.note: Philip is chosen as one of the Seven.
He proclaims Christ in Samaria; many believe, including Simon the magician.
On the desert road to Gaza he explains Isaiah 53 to the Ethiopian and baptizes him.
Philip is found at Azotus (Ashdod) and preaches in the coastal towns.
He settles in Caesarea; years later Paul stays with him and his four prophesying daughters.

title: Peter in Acts
summary: Peter leads the Jerusalem church, visits Samaria and the coastal plain, opens the door to Gentiles at Caesarea, escapes Herod Agrippa, and later appears at Antioch. Tradition places his death in Rome.

stops.note: Pentecost sermon and leadership of the early church.
With John he lays hands on the Samaritan believers.
He heals the paralyzed Aeneas.
He raises Dorcas (Tabitha) and receives the vision of the sheet.
He preaches to Cornelius' household and the Spirit falls on Gentiles.
Imprisoned by Herod Agrippa I and freed by an angel; later speaks at the council.
Paul rebukes him at Antioch for withdrawing from Gentile tables.
Tradition (1 Clement, Eusebius) says he ministered and was martyred in Rome; 1 Peter is sent from "Babylon," often read as Rome.

title: Paul's conversion and early years
summary: Saul of Tarsus, trained in Jerusalem, sets out to arrest believers in Damascus, meets the risen Jesus, spends time in Arabia, returns to Damascus, visits Jerusalem, and goes home to Tarsus until Barnabas brings him to Antioch.

stops.note: Born in Tarsus of Cilicia, a Roman citizen.
Educated under Gamaliel; approves Stephen's death and ravages the church.
Struck down on the road, blinded, and baptized by Ananias.
He goes away into Arabia (probably Nabatea) before returning to Damascus.
He preaches and escapes in a basket over the wall.
Three years after his conversion he visits Peter for fifteen days; Barnabas vouches for him.
Sent off to Tarsus; he works in Syria and Cilicia.
Barnabas brings him to Antioch, where they teach for a year.

title: Paul's first missionary journey
summary: Sent out by the Antioch church (c. AD 46–48), Barnabas and Saul cross Cyprus, then plant churches in the cities of southern Galatia before retracing their steps and reporting how God "opened a door of faith to the Gentiles."

stops.note: The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul; they sail via Seleucia.
They preach in the synagogues of Salamis.
The proconsul Sergius Paulus believes; Elymas the magician is blinded. Saul is now called Paul.
John Mark leaves them and returns to Jerusalem.
Paul's synagogue sermon; turning to the Gentiles after Jewish opposition.
A great number believe, but a plot to stone them forces them out.
A lame man is healed; the crowd hails them as gods, then Paul is stoned and left for dead.
Many disciples are made.
They return, strengthening the disciples and appointing elders.
Return visit to encourage the church.
Return visit: "through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God."
They speak the word in Perga and go down to Attalia.
They report to the church and stay a long time.

title: Paul's second missionary journey
summary: After parting from Barnabas, Paul takes Silas through Asia Minor, adds Timothy, and is called by a vision into Macedonia. Churches are founded in Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea and Corinth (c. AD 49–52).

stops.note: Paul and Barnabas part over John Mark; Paul chooses Silas.
Revisiting the churches with the council's decisions.
Timothy joins the team.
Forbidden by the Spirit to speak in Asia, they pass through Phrygia and Galatia.
The vision of the man of Macedonia; the "we" passages begin.
Lydia is baptized; Paul and Silas are beaten and jailed, and the jailer believes.
Three Sabbaths in the synagogue; a riot drives them out.
The Bereans examine the scriptures daily.
Paul speaks at the Areopagus about the unknown god.
Eighteen months with Priscilla and Aquila; Gallio dismisses the case (AD 51–52). Paul writes 1–2 Thessalonians.
Paul cuts his hair because of a vow and sails.
A brief visit; Priscilla and Aquila remain.
He lands at Caesarea and goes up to greet the church (Jerusalem).
Return to Antioch.

title: Paul's third missionary journey
summary: Paul spends nearly three years at Ephesus, revisits Macedonia and Greece, gathers the collection for Jerusalem, and sails for Jerusalem despite warnings of chains (c. AD 53–57).

stops.note: Paul sets out again.
He strengthens the disciples throughout Galatia and Phrygia.
Two years in the hall of Tyrannus; the silversmiths' riot. He writes 1 Corinthians.
He encourages the churches of Macedonia and writes 2 Corinthians.
Three months in Greece; he writes Romans.
He keeps the Days of Unleavened Bread at Philippi.
Eutychus falls from a window during Paul's long talk and is restored.
Paul walks overland and rejoins the ship.
Sailing down the coast.
Farewell to the Ephesian elders.
Brief stop.
They change ships for Phoenicia.
Disciples urge him through the Spirit not to go on to Jerusalem.
At Philip's house Agabus binds himself with Paul's belt.
Paul meets James and the elders and is arrested in the temple.

title: Paul's voyage to Rome
summary: Having appealed to Caesar, Paul sails under guard from Caesarea, survives a storm and shipwreck on Malta, and reaches Rome, where he lives two years under house arrest (c. AD 59–62).

stops.note: Paul appeals to Caesar before Festus and Agrippa II hears his defense.
The centurion Julius lets Paul visit friends.
They reach Fair Havens on Crete late in the season; Paul warns against sailing on.
A northeaster drives the ship from the coast of Crete.
Shipwreck; Paul survives a viper bite and heals Publius' father. They winter three months.
Three days in Syracuse.
They wait for a south wind.
Believers host them for seven days.
Christians from Rome come out to meet Paul, and he takes courage.
Two years in his own rented house, proclaiming the kingdom unhindered.

title: The spread of the gospel in Acts
summary: Acts follows the commission of Acts 1:8 outward from Jerusalem to Judea and Samaria, to Gentiles at Caesarea and Antioch, across Asia Minor and Greece, and finally to Rome.

stops.note: Pentecost: the church is born among Jews from every nation.
Philip preaches in Samaria after Stephen's death.
Peter preaches to Cornelius, the first Gentile household.
Greeks believe; the disciples are first called Christians; the mission base for Paul.
First missionary journey begins on Cyprus.
Churches in the cities of southern Galatia.
The gospel enters Europe.
A large church in a cosmopolitan port city.
"All the residents of Asia heard the word of the Lord."
Paul proclaims the kingdom at the heart of the empire; a church already existed there.

title: Beyond Acts: traditions of the apostolic mission
summary: Church traditions, not the New Testament, describe the gospel reaching Egypt, Ethiopia and India in the first centuries. These routes are flagged as tradition; their reliability varies.

stops.note: Starting point of the apostolic mission.
Tradition (Eusebius, Church History 2.16) makes John Mark the founder of the church in Alexandria. Not stated in scripture.
Acts records the baptism of an Ethiopian court official; the Aksumite kingdom's conversion came later through Frumentius (4th century, per Rufinus).
The Acts of Thomas and the St. Thomas Christians of Kerala hold that the apostle Thomas preached in India and was martyred near Chennai. Historians are divided on the claim.
Tradition (Irenaeus) places the apostle John's later ministry in Ephesus.
